City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
February 6, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:00 p.m. , on February 6, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on February 03, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
None
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley
INVOCATION: Council Member Leckness
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employee (Assistant City Manager.) The City’s Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. Council Member Schlicht arrived at 5:04 p.m. The City Council reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council provided direction to staff and the Assistant City Manager agreement will be brought back for consideration, in open session, at the next City Council Meeting.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition
Mayor Ury presented certificates of commendation to Sergeant Artur Shvartsberg, Lance Corporal Kayla M. Thompson, Lance Corporal Kyle A. Bond, and Sergeant Randy J. Tapia,
P2.
Recognize the 2011 Employees of the Year
Mayor Ury presented plaques to (1) Public Services Contracts Administrator, Daniel Hernandez, City of Mission Viejo Employee of the Year; (2) Deputy Sheriff II/K-9 Handler, Jarrett Kurimay, Orange County Sheriff’s Department Employee of the Year; and (3) Fire Captain, Brad Haldeman, Orange County Fire Authority Employee of the Year.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Carol Weidler: announced that a state of the art blind rehabilitation center at the Long Beach Veterans Hospital was recently named in honor of Major Charles Robert Soltes, Jr., a fallen soldier whose parents reside in Mission Viejo.
Carolyn Emery, Assistant Executive Officer for the Local Agency Formation Commission: provided an update on LAFCO’s county-wide activities. She also discussed LAFCO’s municipal services review and Mission Viejo’s sphere of influence. Peter Schelden, Mission Viejo Patch: invited residents to a Mayor’s breakfast on Saturday, February 11, 2012, at 8:30 a.m. at Paul’s Pantry. Coffee and pastries will be provided by Patch.com. Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: shared her support for the proposal to give businesses the same benefit of the building permit amnesty program. She also expressed support for LAFCO’s program which allows local governments to share information and resources.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
(1) Approved the Minutes for the Regular City Council Meeting of January 16, 2012, as presented; and (2) approved the Minutes for the Regular/Adjourned City Council Meeting of January 25, 2012, as presented.
3.
Check Register dated January 6, 2012, in the Amount of $807,956.14
Ratified the accompanying check register.
6.
Records for Electronic Retention â?? Public Works
Adopted Resolution 12-07 Authorizing and Directing the City Clerk to Destroy the Original Formats of Certain City Records and Documents that have been Electronically Imaged Pursuant to the Government Code of the State of California.
7.
General Plan Progress Report for 2011
Received and filed report.
9.
2012 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo
Approved the request submitted by Pelican Coast Events LLC to hold the 2012 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, May 20, 2012.
10.
La Paz Bridge and Road Widening (CIP 756)
(1) Approved the easement acquisition agreement at a cost of $259,400.00 and accepted the associated easement deeds; and (2) authorized the City Clerk to record the easement deeds in the office of the County Recorder.
11.
Renewal of City's Communication Circuit Leases
Approved entering into multi-year agreements and issuing of purchase orders to Cox Business in the amount of $114,000.
NEW BUSINESS
16.
Legislative Platform
Heather Stratman and Cori Williams, Townsend Public Affairs: discussed Mission Viejo’s proposed legislative platform in response to State and Federal legislative issues. They further outlined suggested amendments which arose after the agenda materials were published:
1. Page 3, item 1 under pension reform. This item was under wrong category and will be moved up to the local government finance section.
2. Page 4, electronic commerce. This this was carried over from a previous edition and staff has recommended deleting it from the legislative platform. 3. Page 6, housing, community and economic development. Clarified that item 4 is in reference to opportunities that may arise when multiple cities participate in cost saving measures by pooling resources. It is meant for future opportunities that may occur with potential partnerships and cooperative agreements. 4. Page 6, redevelopment. Staff recommends amending this section to reflect new and future legislation that may be introduced to address economic development. 5. Page 7, public safety. The consultant is waiting to receive input from the Mission Viejo police services department.
Ms. Williams answered questions of the City Council regarding the Amazon sales tax which will go into effect in September 2012.
Council Member Schlicht asked for staff to provide additional information on Smart Growth legislation at a later meeting. She also stated that if redevelopment agencies come back, she would like the City to push for voter approval.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approved the Proposed 2011-2012 Legislative Platform, as amended.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
PUBLIC HEARINGS
14.
Proposed Ordinance designating Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones within the City of Mission Viejo as Recommended by the California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection. The Proposed Ordinance will impact Several Areas Along the City's Eastern Boundary, and Areas Northerly of the Foothill Transportation Corridor (SR 241) and in Vicinity of El Toro Road
Mayor Ury announced that his home is very close to one of the affected high fire hazard area zones and therefore he will recuse himself from the discussion and vote.
Council Member Leckness announced that his home is in the very high fire hazard zone and he too recused himself.
At the hour of 6:54 p.m., Mayor Ury turned the meeting over to Mayor Pro Tem Reardon and he and Council Member Leckness left the room.
Director of Community Development Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.
Deputy Fire Marshall Brett Petroff, OCFA: provided a history of very high fire hazard severity zones within cities, the relationship between vegetation and homes during a fire, and the criteria and the purpose of the very high fire hazard severity zone maps.
At the hour of 7:34 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon opened the public hearing.
The following requested that this item be continued so that all affected homeowners can be notified of the public hearing. The speakers provided additional coments regarding the potential negative impact on homeowners insurance policies if a home is in the very high fire hazard zone: Bill Burnham, M.V.; Blake Pickering, M.V.; Joel Sugg, M.V.; Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.; and Curt Stidham, M.V.
The following presented a written comment in favor of adopting only the mandated very high fire hazard areas: Wendy Bucknum, M.V.
Chief Robinson and Deputy Fire Marshall Petroff answered questions of the City Council.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
RECUSE:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury.
RECESS
At the hour of 8:53 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
12.
Youth Services Program Contract
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.
Cameron Harding, SVUSD: answered the City Council Members questions regarding the Kids Factory program.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to extend the contract with the Saddleback Valley Unified School District (SVUSD) Department of Recreation and Community Services to provide Youth Services Programs through Fiscal Year 2012-13 in the amount of $712,000.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
17.
One Appointment Each to the Investment Advisory Commission and the Planning and Transportation Commission
Council Member Kelley announced that she will defer her appointment to the next meeting.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Ury, to appoint Stella Guinta to serve on the Planning and Transportation Commission.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR (Continued)
4.
Check Register dated January 13, 2012 in the amount of $1,057,479.69
Council Member Schlicht inquired about the payment made to Jim Leach and Company for Mission Viejo Television consultant services.
City Manager Wilberg responded that Mr. Leach is under contract to assist the City on an as-needed basis. His first assignment was to help with the transition from the Cox Franchise to the State Franchise and he further assisted with getting through the red tape at Cox to bring cable service into the Marguerite Tennis Center facility, which is currently under construction.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Mayor Ury, to ratify the accompanying check register.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
5.
Check Register dated January 20, 2012 in the amount of $757,062.45
Council Member Schlicht asked about a payment made to Outdoor Sign Systems for ten desktop display signs.
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay responded that the signs are used to direct visitors within City facilities.
Council Member Schlicht asked what service Solar World Wide, LLC provides for the City.
Mr. Rattay announced that he is not familiar with the company and he will get back to the Council when he has details on the company and the service they provide.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to ratify the accompanying check register.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
8.
Annual Police Services Motorcycle Maintenance Contract Amendment
Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report and described the City’s attempt to obtain a competitive maintenance contract for the Police Services motorcycles.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve the First Amendment to the existing contract with Huntington Beach Honda Motorcycles to increase the contract from $30,000 to an amount not to exceed $65,000.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
13.
Cabot/Camino Capistrano Bridge Improvements (CIP 782)
Council Member Schlicht stated that she believes three of the Council Members don't understand the need for this bridge and she expressed concern with the funds that are being expended on the project. Director of Public Works Chagnon described the bridge improvement project and stated that it is included in the Master Plan of Arterial Highways. The project will be funded with 80% federal dollars and the City’s portion will be primarily funded with GMA monies designated for that area of the City.
Council Member Schlicht stated that she was hoping to get some sort of report on the need for project, how it got started, and who will benefit the most.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to authorize the approval of Change Order 3 to Purchase Order 050251 for additional preliminary engineering services in the amount of $84,709 to RBF Consulting, Inc.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
OLD BUSINESS
15.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) approve Change Order No.6 to the Construction Contract with Western Alta Construction Company in an amount not to exceed $35,817.71; and (2) adopt Resolution 12-08 Amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 Budget for Costs Related to Capital Improvement Marguerite Tennis Center Project 501 for $28,830.00.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS (Continued)
18.
Appointment to the Orange County Vector Control District
Mayor Ury re-appointed John Paul Ledesma to serve on the Orange County Vector Control District Board of Directors for a two-year term.
19.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: stated that Orange County Employees Retirement System (OCERS) is not earning the 7.75% return on their investment as expected and that has an affect on the OCFA budget. He further questioned the amount of money that the cities are contributing to OCFA and he requested a copy of the City's contract with OCFA.
20.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Council Member Leckness announced that he had nothing to report.
21.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the report.
22.
SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report
Council Member Kelley presented the report.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager’s Report
City Attorney’s Report
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
23.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Kelley stated that it was wonderful to recognize the employees of the year at the beginning of the meeting and she congratulated City Employee Daniel Hernandez, Deputy Sheriff II/K-9 Handler, Jarrett Kurimay and Fire Captain, Brad Haldeman. Council Member Kelley announced that she attended the Wounded Warriors Softball Tournament and it took her breath away to see the wounded warriors play. She stated that it was a good reminder that freedom is not free and it was a powerful picture of determination and perseverance. She further noted that nothing was stopping those young men and she is very proud of her City for hosting the event and providing facilities. Council Member Kelley announced that the Community of Character word for the month of February is unity.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness thanked Keith Rattay for transforming the Council Chamber into a phenomenal stage for last weekend’s Lord of the Strings concert with Jeff Peterson. He also thanked his Council colleagues for supporting his nomination of the new Planning and Transportation Commissioner, Stella Guinta.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht recognized the employees of the year and thanked Daniel Hernandez for his hard work at the City facilities. She also thanked Deputy Jarrett Kurimay and Fire Captain Brad Haldemans and she stated that Mission Viejo’s safety officers continue to do a wonderful job for the City. Council Member Schlicht announced that she attended the January 23 American Legion Post 862 meeting where high school student Christopher Delpadre was recognized for his participation in the American Legion’s National High School Oratorical Contest. She also attended a portion of the January 28 Elks Club celebration for local safety officers. In conclusion, Council Member Schlicht reminded residents that South Coast Outreach is always in need of supplies and currently, they are seeking donations of peanut butter, breakfast cereal and tuna.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon echoed her colleague’s comments about the employees of the year and she announced that city staffer Daniel Hernandez plans to move back to Mexico when he retires. Mr. Hernandez would like to run for Mayor in his home town and to pattern his work from the things he has learned in Mission Viejo. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she too attended the Wounded Warriors Amputee Softball Game and she took her grandsons so they could see what it has cost some of our military personnel to provide for our freedoms. She stated that it was a great experience and she really appreciated Mayor Ury’s commitment to make it an annual event. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon also discussed her attendance at the Elks Club safety officer recognition dinner where she enjoyed seeing Jarrett Kurimay and Brad Haldemans honored. She further announced that the Mission Viejo YMCA’s campaign kick-off fundraiser starts tomorrow and every penny that they raise will help a child in need. She also encouraged residents to acquaint themselves with the rather serious concerns that surround the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Ury announced that resident Chuck Costello’s wife, Maridon, passed away last week and she asked for prayers on his behalf and for young Cade Spinello.
Mayor Ury
24.
Commercial Building Permit Fee Program
Mayor Ury presented his report.
Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Leckness, to authorize staff to implement the commercial building permit fee program outlined in this staff report; and authorize staff to make appropriate budget adjustments to reduce budgeted revenue for FY 2011/12 for the implementation of the commercial building permit fee program in the amount of $66,000.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
None
Mayor Ury noted that it was wonderful to attend the Wounded Warriors Softball Game. It really put things into perspective and demonstrated that freedom is not free. He announced that he will be speaking at the Casta del Sol Lincoln Day luncheon on February 12 at noon and then he’ll speak at Kaleidoscope’s tribute to our nation’s service men and women at 1:45 p.m. Mayor Ury also reminded residents that The Mission Viejo Patch is sponsoring Breakfast with the Mayor at Paul’s Pantry on Saturday, February 11 at 8:30 a.m.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 10:04 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Monday, February 20, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of February 20, 2012
